name: Deflicker
description: Even out brightness pulsing between frames
longDescription:
Film shot on a cine camera often pulses in brightness, because the shutter and the film advance were never perfectly in step. Scanned, that pulsing survives as a flicker that is far more obvious on a screen than it ever was on a projector.

"Whole frame" is the one to reach for: it measures each frame's exposure against its neighbours and corrects both the brightness and the contrast. It removes about 83% of typical cine flicker.

"Across the frame" handles the case where different parts of the picture flicker differently, which the whole-frame measurement cannot see. It is gentler and less complete; use it when the first option leaves something behind.

Runs after deinterlacing and before the cleanup passes, which all assume the exposure is steady.

methods.name: Whole frame
methods.description: Corrects each frame's overall exposure against its neighbours — the usual cine-film case

methods.name: Across the frame
methods.description: For flicker that varies from one part of the picture to another

ui.label: Method
ui.description: Whole-frame is the usual choice for scanned film.

ui.label: Strength
ui.description: Lower this if the correction is over-eager on a shot with a genuine brightness change, like a lamp being switched on.

ui.label: Frames compared
ui.description: How many frames either side are averaged to decide what the exposure should have been.

ui.label: Strength
ui.description: Higher compares against more distant frames.

ui.label: Aggressive
ui.description: Corrects harder, at more risk of smearing genuine movement.
